items.title: Deep ultraviolet gallium-oxide avalanche photodiodes reaching an impulse-response-derived gain-bandwidth record of 152 GHz
items.abstract: Abstract Solar-blind Ga 2 O 3 -based photodetectors, sensing deep ultraviolet (DUV) light (200–280 nm), offer unparalleled opportunities for secure non-line-of-sight optical communication. Yet their practical applications have been largely hindered by the relatively low gain-bandwidth product (GBP), due to the fundamental trade-off between response speed and photoelectric gain. Here, we report nanosecond-level-response solar-blind avalanche photodetectors based on β-Ga 2 O 3 /MgO/La 0.8 Ca 0.2 MnO 3 (LCMO) n-Barrier-p heterojunctions with high apparent gain over 2.6×10 6 , thereby achieving an impulse-response-derived record-breaking 152 GHz gain-bandwidth product — outpacing the state-of-the-art Ga 2 O 3 -based devices by 3 orders of magnitude. The MgO interlayer enables lattice matching and engineered conduction band offset to boost gain and suppress dark current, while the p-type LCMO layer introduces a large valence band offset and simultaneously establishes a hole-selective transport highway for ultrafast response. This work not only resolves the longstanding gain-bandwidth trade-off in DUV photodetection but also presents a universal band-engineering framework for next-generation optoelectronics.

items.title: A highly distorted benzenium cation
items.abstract: Abstract In contrast to the well-explored peripheral functionalization of benzene, its skeletal alteration remains underdeveloped. Here, we report a highly distorted benzenium cation, 2,3-dihydroxy-1,4,6-triamino-5-nitrobenzenium (TANBC + ), featuring a ring twist angle of 35.91° and a ring C-C bond length of 1.540 Å, both rank the highest among all benzenium cations. Such pronounced structural distortions endow TANBC + with unique electronic properties, including a highly positive electrostatic charge on the warped carbon, weak aromaticity, and a low ring bond dissociation energy. Consequently, instead of undergoing peripheral functionalization like typical benzenium cations, TANBC + participates in three distinct benzene ring reconstruction pathways or remains inert under standard electrophilic substitution conditions. Moreover, despite its distorted structure, TANBC + exhibits excellent ambient stability, stabilized by extensive hydrogen bonding, and can be synthesized readily without harsh conditions usually required for conventional benzenium cations. This work not only introduces a new strategy for benzene reconstruction but also redefines the role of benzenium cations from mediators of peripheral functionalization to promoters of skeletal alteration, thereby advancing the fundamental chemistry of benzene.

items.title: Greenhouse gas responses to coastal wetland land use change vary by ecosystem and conversion pathway
items.abstract: Abstract Land-use and land-cover change (LULCC) is altering greenhouse gas (GHG) dynamics in coastal wetlands, yet how these responses vary among ecosystems and conversion pathways remains uncertain. Here, we synthesized 276 studies and applied multilevel meta-analysis to paired LULCC comparisons. GHG responses varied with pre-conversion wetland type, destination land use, hydrology, and soil carbon and nitrogen status. Pooled sustained-flux global warming potential (SGWP) was ‒122.41 ± 81.99 mg CO 2 e m ‒2 h ‒1 for natural coastal wetlands and 250.60 ± 101.06 for LULCC sites, corresponding to 0.17 ± 0.06 Gt CO 2 e of cumulative emissions over two decades. The descriptive SGWP contrast with pooled LULCC sites was larger for vegetated wetlands ( + 309.32%) than for tidal flats ( + 165.02%). Ecologically restored wetlands showed negative pooled SGWP ( − 33.03 ± 114.70 mg CO 2 e m ‒2 h ‒1 ), contrasting with the positive pooled LULCC estimate. Our results indicate that GHG responses to coastal wetland conversion are ecosystem- and pathway-specific, underscoring the importance of conserving vegetated wetlands and targeting restoration.

items.title: Early-life skin molecular signatures are predictive of atopic dermatitis risk in an Asian preconception birth cohort
Entropy-engineered polar heterogeneity enables near-decoupled polarization–strain behavior for high-density energy storage
Mapping temperature using transmission Kikuchi diffraction
items.abstract: Abstract As electronic devices are engineered at increasingly smaller length scales, new nanoscopic metrologies are needed. Measuring nanoscale temperatures and pressures is challenging as physical contact inevitably perturbs the system, and collecting far-field thermal radiation limits the spatial resolution. Kikuchi diffraction thermometry (KDTh), a non-contact scanning electron microscope (SEM) technique, can sensitively map nanoscale temperatures. Local lattice changes measured by Kikuchi pattern fitting enable translating volumetric strain to temperature via the material’s coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE). Measurements on Joule-heated graphite come from rastering a 5.5-nm electron probe across the sample, achieving a ~ 0.01% fractional precision and 2.2 K/ $$\sqrt{{{\rm{Hz}}}}$$ Hz temperature sensitivity. KDTh offers superior sensitivity by fitting the entire Kikuchi pattern, instead of a particular Kikuchi band or interband angle. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) techniques can achieve a similar precision, but electron-transparency limits their applications. KDTh can operate in both transmission and reflection modes to cost-effectively accommodate a variety of samples.

Visible light drives bright extreme-ultraviolet high harmonics
items.last_author_affiliation: GSI Helmholtzzentrum für Schwerionenforschung, Darmstadt, Germany.; Helmholtz Institute Jena, Jena, Germany.; Institute of Applied Physics, Friedrich Schiller University Jena, Jena, Germany.; Fraunhofer Institute for Applied Optics and Precision Engineering, Jena, Germany.
items.abstract: Abstract Coherent extreme-ultraviolet (XUV) light is a central tool in modern photon science, probing the electronic, chemical and structural properties of matter. High-harmonic generation can extend the reach of laser sources into this spectral range, but the achievable photon flux falls sharply as photon energy increases. We show experimentally and theoretically that plasma-core-induced self-guiding of a visible-wavelength driver in helium sustains high intensity and favorable phase matching over an extended propagation length. We achieve a conversion efficiency of up to 10 −6 in a single high-harmonic line and phase-matched emission extending to 100 eV. With less than 10 W of average power at 516 nm from a frequency-doubled ytterbium laser, we generate 1.8 × 10 11 photons s −1 within 2 % bandwidth at 13.5 nm (91.8 eV), exceeding previous reports by more than an order of magnitude. These results establish a power-scalable XUV platform for actinic metrology, spectroscopy and coherent imaging.

items.title: Chronically stable, frequency-selective auditory brainstem stimulation via ultra-flexible penetrating electrode arrays
items.abstract: Abstract The auditory brainstem implant (ABI) targeting the cochlear nucleus (CN) can restore hearing in patients ineligible for cochlear implants. However, conventional ABI using surface electrode array yields highly variable outcomes, from poor to moderate, due to limited spatial resolution and restricted tonotopic access. Here, we developed a penetrating ABI based on a high-density, ultra-flexible implantable neural electrode array (uFINE). In normal-hearing rats, uFINE mapped frequency tuning from 0.5 to 32 kHz in CN and the inferior colliculus (IC). Selective CN stimulation via uFINE evoked IC responses closely matching acoustic tonotopy, with IC tuning widths comparable to tone-evoked responses, and these remained stable for over 136 days, with minimal gliosis observed. Daily sequential CN–IC microstimulation progressively shifted the location of the CN-evoked IC response peak toward the targeted IC stimulation site, consistent with use-dependent plasticity. Together, these findings demonstrate that uFINE enables high-resolution, tonotopically precise, and long-term stable CN stimulation across a broad frequency range with minimal tissue disruption, highlighting its potential to enhance ABI-mediated hearing restoration.

items.title: Landscape fire sourced PM2.5, cause-specific paediatric hospitalisations, and the role of tree cover
Influenza A virus orchestrates ciliated cell fate and injury during the mucociliary damage repair cycle
items.abstract: Abstract Influenza A virus causes acute damage to airway epithelium, yet the damage–repair cycle and mechanisms underlying persistent mucociliary clearance (MCC) dysfunction long after viral clearance remain unclear. Here, using longitudinal in vivo quantitative micro-optical coherence tomography, we show that global MCC impairment persists for more than 14 days, marked by impaired ciliary activity and sustained mucus hypersecretion in male mice infected with the H1N1 influenza A/Puerto Rico/8/1934 (PR8) strain. Through lineage tracing and multi-omics analyses, we identify an immune-mediated transdifferentiation program in which IFN signaling activates the IDO1–AhR axis to drive ciliated-to-mucous cell fate transition and chronic muco-obstruction after H1N1 PR8 infection in a reconstructed human bronchial epithelium model. In parallel, we identify the viral M2 protein as a key driver of ciliary loss, suppressing the host TP73–FOXJ1–RFX3 regulatory axis and promoting proteasomal degradation of FOXJ1. Together, these findings uncover host- and virus-driven pathways that cooperatively impair airway epithelial homeostasis and sustain MCC failure beyond active infection, highlighting therapeutic targets for post-influenza muco-obstructive disease.

items.title: A global atlas of digital dermatology to map innovation and disparities
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence promises democratized access to dermatological care, but model reliability depends on the quality and comprehensiveness of the underlying data. Despite rapid growth in publicly available dermatology images, the field lacks quantitative indicators to measure whether new datasets expand clinical coverage or merely replicate what is already known. Existing collections are widely assumed to be biased, yet the scale and topography of these gaps have remained unquantified, leaving the community without a road map for strategic data acquisition. Here, we show, by unifying 1.1 million images from 29 public datasets into a queryable semantic atlas, that the global archive is markedly skewed and increasingly redundant: darker skin tones (Fitzpatrick V–VI) constitute only 11.0% of images, pediatric patients only 2.3%, and informational novelty has plateaued despite exponential growth, revealing where targeted data acquisition is most needed.

items.title: [c2]Daisy-chain molecular turing machines with switchable fluorescence outputs
Episodic memory consolidation by reactivation of human concept neurons during sleep reflects contents, not sequence of events
items.abstract: Abstract How do our brains manage to store our everyday experiences into memory? Neurons in the human temporal lobe that respond to the concept of an individual person or object have been shown to provide the semantic building blocks for episodic memory. Recording from 1415 neurons in neurosurgical patients who learned a story involving specific concepts, we found reactivation of neurons representing these concepts during slow-wave sleep after learning. Concept neurons were conjointly reactivated, particularly during sharp-wave ripples, with time lags suitable for synaptic modification. However, the temporal sequence of reactivation did not reflect the sequence of concepts in the learned story. Unlike rodent place cells, which can acquire preferred firing locations during exploration of new environments according to their pre-existing preferred sequence of activation, human concept neurons are tuned to specific semantic contents before learning starts. Consequently, pre-existing firing sequences correlate with consecutive place fields in rodents, but not with sequences of events in human experience. Thus, in contrast to reactivation of rodent place cells, reactivation of human concept cells does not reflect sequences of events in human experience.

items.title: G3BP1-induced retrograde transport blockade triggers HSC activation and liver fibrosis via COPI alternative splicing
Accelerating high-throughput catalyst screening by direct generation of equilibrium adsorption structures
items.abstract: Abstract The adsorption energy serves as a crucial descriptor for the large-scale screening of catalysts. Nevertheless, the limited distribution of training data for the extensively utilised machine learning interatomic potential, predominantly sourced from near-equilibrium structures, results in unreliable adsorption structures and consequent adsorption energy predictions. In this context, we present DBCata, a deep generative model that integrates a periodic Brownian-bridge framework with an equivariant graph neural network to establish a low-dimensional transition manifold between unrelaxed and DFT-relaxed structures, without requiring explicit energy or force information. Upon training, DBCata effectively generates high-fidelity adsorption geometries, achieving an interatomic distance mean absolute error of 0.035 Å on the dataset from Catalysis-Hub, which is approximately 70% lower than that of the current state-of-the-art machine learning potential models. Moreover, the corresponding DFT accuracy can be improved within 0.1 eV in 94% of instances by identifying and refining anomalous predictions through a hybrid chemical-heuristic and self-supervised outlier detection approach. We demonstrate that DBCata enables accelerated high-throughput computational screening for alloy catalysts in the oxygen reduction reaction, highlighting the potential of DBCata as a powerful tool for catalyst design and optimisation.

items.title: Epiformer: epistasis detection by genome language model and dual-channel network.
items.last_author_affiliation: School of Software, Shandong University, Jinan, 250101, China. gxyu@sdu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Epistasis plays a crucial role in explaining missing heritability in complex traits, yet most detection methods fail to effectively capture local and global interaction patterns and long-range dependencies critical to complex trait architecture. We propose Epiformer that leverages genome language model Evo 2 to capture long-range dependencies from genetic background, and a dual-channel network to jointly model local and global epistasis and additive effects. Epiformer can identify key SNPs and their interactions from complex genomic data to empower phenotype prediction with interpretability, which reinforces epistasis detection. Epiformer performs robustly across species, revealing biologically meaningful patterns and offering new insights into genetic architecture.

items.title: flexiAsCas12a and other Cas12a variants enhance the applicability of Cas12a nucleases in prime editing.
items.last_author_affiliation: Institute of Molecular Life Sciences, Research Centre of Natural Sciences, Hungarian Research Network, Budapest, H-1117, Hungary. toth.eszter.enzim@ttk.hu.; Pannon Plazmid Kft., Budapest, H-1114, Hungary. toth.eszter.enzim@ttk.hu.
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Amongst the genome manipulation tools based on the versatile CRISPR-Cas system, prime editing is the most prominent one as a method that enables precise insertions, deletions, and substitutions without inducing double-strand breaks. Cas12a nucleases are widely used for genome editing and nucleic acid detection, owing to their unique properties; however, their relatively long PAM requirements limit their applicability. RESULTS: We develop PAM-flexible Cas12a variants capable of functioning effectively within mammalian cells, thereby enabling the cleavage of targets previously inaccessible to Cas12a nucleases. Amongst the Lb-, As-, Mb-, and FnCas12a variants we develop, flexiAsCas12a (AsCas12a with flexible PAM recognition) is the most effective, expanding the range of recognized PAM sequences by Cas12a variants to include NATN, NCCN and GTCN sequences. Using the currently available Cas12a variants with relaxed PAM recognition (impLbCas12a, flexiAsCas12a, and enAsCas12a), we develop circular RNA-guided split prime editors and validate their functionality on non-canonical PAM sequences. CONCLUSIONS: flexiAsCas12a joins the repertoire of Cas12a PAM variants, enabling access to an increasing number of target sequences by Cas12a nucleases.

items.title: Spatial metabolic ecosystems shape the architecture of IDH-mutant glioma
items.corresponding_institution: Cancer Division, The Walter and Eliza Hall Insitute of Medical Research, Melbourne, Australia
items.abstract: The principles governing tissue organization in IDH-mutant glioma remain poorly understood, particularly in the absence of hypoxia and necrosis that define IDH-wildtype glioblastoma. Here, we integrated spatial transcriptomics, metabolomics and histology across co-registered serial tissue sections, generating a multidimensional atlas of IDH-mutant glioma. Integration with an independent spatial transcriptomics cohort and a single cell atlas (n=101 samples), enabled resolution of metabolic and cellular heterogeneity underlying tissue organization. We identified twelve conserved spatial niches with distinct metabolic identities that could not be explained by cellular composition or histology alone. Beyond these ecosystems, we discovered a transcriptionally and epigenetically intermediate malignant cell state enriched in WHO grade 2/3 oligodendroglioma, and spatially segregated myeloid programs. Importantly, progression following chemoradiotherapy was associated with expansion of a glutathione-rich, NRF2-associated antioxidant niche. Together, our findings establish metabolic specialization as a fundamental dimension of glioma organization, providing new insight into tumor heterogeneity, progression and treatment-associated adaptation.

items.title: A Novel Autoantibody against LAG-3 in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Gastroenterology and Hepatology, Kyoto University Graduate School of Medicine, Kyoto, Japan
items.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is an autoimmune disease characterized by immune tolerance loss, although its pathogenesis remains incompletely understood. Immune checkpoint molecules maintain peripheral tolerance, and their dysregulation contributes to autoimmunity. Autoantibodies against lymphocyte activation gene-3 (LAG-3), an immune checkpoint molecule, were identified in a subset of patients with SLE. We enrolled 130 patients with SLE, 119 patients with other autoimmune diseases, and 32 healthy controls. The sera of patients with SLE were screened for antibodies against various immune checkpoint molecules to identify clinically relevant disease-specific autoantibodies against LAG-3. Functional assays were performed to assess the effect of anti-LAG-3 autoantibodies on the interaction between LAG-3 and major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class II. Pathogenic relevance was evaluated using genetic deletion and immunization-based mouse models. Anti-LAG-3 autoantibodies were detected in 52/130 patients with SLE (40.0%) but only 4 of 119 patients with other autoimmune diseases (3.4%). These autoantibodies were associated with lupus nephritis and higher disease activity. In mice, Lag3 deletion or human LAG-3 immunization induced lupus-like autoimmunity. These findings support the clinical relevance of anti-LAG-3 autoantibodies in SLE and implicate LAG-3 checkpoint disruption in lupus-like autoimmunity.

items.title: TrES-seq integrates single-cell RNA and nanobody-based histone mark profiles to decode epigenetic and transcriptional axes of cell identity
items.corresponding_institution: Swiss Institute for Experimental Cancer Research (ISREC), School of Life Sciences, EPFL, Lausanne, Switzerland
items.abstract: Histone post-translational modifications and gene expression jointly shape cellular identity and activity. However, systematically assessing their heterogeneity and functional interdependence requires high-quality multimodal single-cell readouts, whose generation still faces significant technological challenges. Here, we developed TrES-seq (transcriptional and epigenetic state sequencing), a method that integrates scRNA-seq with species-specific nanobody Tn5 fusion proteins to jointly profile RNA and two histone modifications in the same cells and across multiple samples. In human tonsils, single-cell H3K27ac, H3K27me3, H3K9me3, and RNA data in >25,000 cells revealed a one-to-many relationship where heterogeneous transcriptional states shared similar epigenetic profiles. For example, naive and memory B cells were transcriptionally different but epigenetically indistinguishable, while the epigenetic status of enhancers but not promoters separated germinal center from naive and memory B cells. Moreover, naturally occurring and treatment-induced cell state transitions revealed broad transcriptional changes occurring among genes that already exhibited and retained an epigenetically active state. Overall, TrES-seq provides a robust and cost-effective platform to determine how epigenetic states influence transcriptional heterogeneity, shaping cell phenotypes and function in different physiological and pathological contexts.

items.title: ADP-ribosylation governs the repair of topoisomerase IIIβ-induced nucleic acid damage
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Pharmacology and Physiology, University of Maryland, School of Medicine, Baltimore, MD 21201, USA
items.abstract: Abortive DNA and RNA-linked covalent cleavage complexes formed by the unique dual-activity human topoisomerase III{beta} (TOP3B) disrupt nucleic acid metabolism and can promote cancer cell death. Here, we identify poly(ADP-ribosylation) (PARylation) as a key pathway that regulates the repair and stability of both DNA- and RNA-linked TOP3B cleavage complexes (TOP3Bccs). We show that accumulated TOP3Bccs undergo rapid PARylation in a PARP1-dependent manner and that this modification is dynamically reversed by poly(ADP-ribose) glycohydrolase (PARG). Mass spectrometry identified major ADP-ribosylation sites on TOP3B, and disruption of these sites impaired TOP3Bcc homeostasis. Mechanistically, PARylation recruits flap endonuclease 1 (FEN1) to excise and repair TOP3Bccs. Persistent PARylation caused by PARG inhibition recruits the deubiquitylating enzyme (DUB) USP10 to promote TOP3Bcc deubiquitylation and thereby stabilize TOP3Bccs, presumably by preventing proteasomal degradation. Together, this study identifies a dynamic PARylation-mediated pathway that coordinates the repair of abortive TOP3Bccs. This pathway defines a critical mechanism of TOP3Bcc homeostasis and may influence cancer cell responses to TOP3B-targeting agents.

items.title: Identification of seven candidate structured noncoding RNA motifs in protists by comparative genomics
items.corresponding_institution: Medical School, College of Materials Science and Engineering, Key Laboratory of Fujian Molecular Medicine, Key Laboratory of Xiamen Marine and Gene Drugs, Key L
items.abstract: Protists represent a highly diverse assemblage of predominantly unicellular eukaryotes, including protozoa, algae, and slime molds. Their essential roles in global ecosystems, along with their significance as human parasites, underscore the need for a deeper understanding of their conserved genetic elements. In this study, we employed an integrated computational approach combining CMfinder and R-scape to systematically identify and evaluate structured non-coding RNA (ncRNA) motifs across protist genomes. Through rigorous assessment and functional annotation, we report seven conserved structured ncRNAs that are likely functional RNA motifs involved in regulating the synthesis of the carbon fixation protein ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase (RuBisCO), the light-harvesting and transfer protein phycocyanin, subunits of photosystems I and II, as well as mRNA splicing regulation. Notably, we also identified a structured ncRNA motif that may possess a dual function, capable of bidirectionally regulating the photosystem genes psaI and psbJ simultaneously. Our findings provide valuable insights into the diversity and functional significance of structured ncRNAs in microbial eukaryotes.

items.title: Quantitative Spatial Analysis of Matrix Remodelling in Wounds Using Digital Pathology and Fractal Analysis
items.corresponding_institution: The University of Manchester, FBMH, School of Biological Sciences
items.abstract: Wound healing involves spatially heterogeneous changes in matrix composition and organisation that can be difficult to capture using qualitative histological assessment alone. We developed a reproducible digital pathology workflow to quantify matrix features in cutaneous wound sections, compare them with unwounded skin, and derive an exploratory Histological Wound Index (HWI). Four normal-skin and six wound sections from patients with underlying vascular disease or diabetes were analysed using QuPath, ImageJ/FracLac and Python as a proof of principle. Approximately 500 x 500 um regions of interest (ROI) were assigned to normal skin, wound centre, proximal edge or distant edge. Collagen, acidic mucins, proteoglycans, glycosaminoglycans (GAGs) and necrotic tissue coverage were quantified using image classifiers and analysed with linear mixed-effects models. Collagen architecture was assessed from collagen-selective binary masks using fractal dimension and lacunarity. Collagen coverage, fractal dimension, mucins coverage, necrosis and lacunarity were z-standardised and integrated into the HWI. Unwounded skin showed high collagen coverage and fractal dimension, with low lacunarity, mucin, proteoglycans, GAGs, and necrosis. In contrast, wound-centre tissue showed low collagen coverage and fractal dimension together with higher mucin, proteoglycans, GAGs, and necrosis. Distant-edge regions retained comparatively normal-like characteristics, whereas proximal-edge regions showed intermediate values. HWI was highest in normal skin and lowest in the wound centre. A descriptive matched-ROI comparison of two wound sections reproduced this regional ordering when all component measures were derived from identical ROI boundaries. This workflow provides a reproducible framework for quantifying regional ECM features and collagen-mask architecture in wound histology. The HWI is an exploratory histological summary requiring validation in larger longitudinal datasets.

items.title: BEguided: Systematic guide and base editor evaluation for precision single-nucleotide editing
items.corresponding_institution: Medical Systems Biology, Faculty of Medicine Carl Gustav Carus, TU Dresden, Dresden, Germany.
items.abstract: Base editing enables precise nucleotide substitutions without introducing DNA double-strand breaks, but identifying optimal editor-guide combinations remains challenging because PAM compatibility, editing-window positioning, bystander modifications, and off-target effects must be considered simultaneously. Here, we introduce BEguided, an integrated computational platform for variant-specific guide RNA design and systematic comparison across 38 predefined base-editor profiles, with support for user-defined editors. BEguided incorporates single-nucleotide variants directly into target sequences, eliminating the need for customized reference genomes, while its companion tool, BEguidedOFF, provides base-editing-aware off-target prediction. To demonstrate the utility of this approach, we systematically assessed the accessibility of the 1,000 most frequent ABE-editable cancer mutations to adenine base editing. Under stringent guide-quality, bystander-editing, and predicted off-target criteria, only 7 mutations could be targeted using SpCas9-ABE8e. Expanding the analysis to additional SpCas9-compatible adenine base editors increased this number to 30, while inclusion of SaCas9, relaxed-PAM Cas9-NG/SpG variants, and PAM-less SpRY further expanded the number of potentially targetable mutations to 100, 156, and 238, respectively. These findings highlight the substantial impact of editor selection on mutation accessibility and establish BEguided as a versatile framework for identifying and prioritizing base-editing strategies for disease-associated variants. BEguided is available at https://beguided.buchholzlab.org.

items.title: Movement refinement and cholinergic regulation of outcome-dependent updating during skilled reaching.
items.abstract: Motor skill learning transforms initially variable actions into precise and reproducible movements. Because conventional measures of task success obscure the distinct processes through which this refinement occurs, we combined detailed outcome scoring and kinematic analysis of single-pellet reaching in mice to resolve how individual components of the action change with repetition. Decomposing reaching into successive stages revealed improvements in targeting and retrieval, while grasp success-rate after pellet contact did not change detectably. Paw trajectories became more consistent across both successful and unsuccessful reaches, whereas changes in the mean speed profile were only detected in successful reaches. To examine how striatal cholinergic signaling contributes to movement refinement and the influence of recent outcomes on subsequent actions, we monitored acetylcholine (ACh) in vivo and inhibited cholinergic interneurons (CINs) during training. ACh was elevated before reach onset and declined during execution across all reach outcomes types. CIN inhibition had little effect on movement refinement across days but altered how recent outcomes influenced the next reach. In control animals, a failed attempt moved the reach away from the animal's practiced successful trajectory but this did not occur after CIN inhibition, most clearly when the pellet had been grasped and then lost. These findings distinguish refinement of the practiced movement from outcome-dependent adjustments to its execution. Together, they raise the possibility that the pre-reach ACh elevation plays a role in enabling the evaluation of recent outcomes to update the execution of the next reach.

items.title: Cross-Species Dynamics of Transposable Elements in Aging Female Visceral Adipose Tissues
items.abstract: Transposable elements (TEs) make up nearly half of mammalian genomes and are increasingly implicated in genomic instability, cellular stress responses, aging, and age-related disease. Recent past research has highlighted their significant involvement in disease models such as cancer and Alzheimer's disease (AD), though much remains to be unraveled regarding these genomic insertions. In this study, we explore the involvement of TEs in aging female mouse and human visceral adipose tissue (VAT) using 10x single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) data analyzed with the computational tool SoloTE. By assessing the TE-annotated snRNA-seq count matrix using Seurat, we found that retrotransposons-specifically short interspersed nuclear elements (SINEs) and long interspersed nuclear elements (LINEs) on chromosomes 1 and 19-are significantly upregulated in aging female human VAT and in potential senescent cells (CDKN1A^+). Although changes in mouse VAT were less pronounced, long terminal repeats (LTRs) were predominant in aging mouse cells. Furthermore, analysis of upregulated features in aging and CDKN1A^+ female human VAT cells revealed that LINE and SINE TEs embedded within specific gene loci-most notably CUX1, SOD2, C3, NAMPT, ALDH1A3, IL6, and the non-coding RNA LOC105375913-exhibit a positive regulatory relationship with their host genes. Specifically, higher TE expression may directly upregulate host gene expression (e.g., C3 TEs driving C3 upregulation). Consistently ranking at the top of differentially expressed feature lists, these TEs act as potential drivers of aging and cellular senescence in female human VAT and can be plausible targets without risk of disruption of multiple biological systems.

items.title: Linking cross-species hemodynamics with neuronal activity in prefrontal cortex during abstract sequence viewing
items.abstract: Humans and other primates have a remarkable ability to identify and predict abstract patterns that evolve through time, but the neural mechanisms that support this capability remain poorly understood. Lateral prefrontal cortex (LPFC) has been implicated in abstract sequence tracking in both humans and macaques, but it is unclear whether underlying processes are shared across species. Further, most existing evidence relies on hemodynamic responses, which can have variable relationships with neuronal activity. We leveraged a combination of human fMRI, monkey fMRI, and electrophysiology to bridge these gaps. We found that humans and macaques show functionally homologous hemodynamic activation in LPFC during abstract sequence viewing, and neuronal responses within fMRI-targeted regions in macaques contain information about abstract and sensory variables in parallel. However, neuronal activity did not directly mirror hemodynamic responses, and abstract sequence responses were found both near and far from fMRI peaks. In contrast, distinct dynamics of spiking activity were selectively present near fMRI peaks, suggesting that temporal coordination across neurons may influence hemodynamic activity in prefrontal cortex. Together, these experiments establish a link between human brain activity, macaque fMRI, and single neuron responses, providing a window into the neural processes that mediate abstract sequence detection.

items.title: Myeloid DNA methyltransferase 3A loss impairs macrophage polarization and promotes inflammation, phagocytosis and hepatosplenomegaly
items.corresponding_institution: Institute of Clinical Molecular Biology (IKMB), Christian-Albrechts-University and University Hospital Schleswig-Holstein, Campus Kiel, 24105, Kiel, Germany.
items.abstract: Background: Genetic variants in the de novo DNA methyltransferase DNMT3A increase inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) risk, yet the mechanisms linking defective DNMT3A to IBD remain unclear. As macrophages gatekeep immune homeostasis, we characterized how myeloid-specific DNMT3A loss affects monocytic differentiation and inflammatory properties. Methods: We generated myeloid-specific Dnmt3a-deficient mice (Dnmt3a-LysM) via LysM-cre. Deletion was confirmed in gut lamina propria CD11b+ cells and bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDM). M1/M2-polarized BMDMs were characterized by methylation profiling, mRNA-sequencing, flow cytometry, arginase/NOS activity, phagocytosis (FITC-zymosan), and co-culture with wounded ModeK epithelial monolayers. Colitis was induced using dextran sodium sulfate (DSS). Results: Dnmt3a expression was induced by M2 and repressed by inflammatory stimuli in wild-type (Dnmt3afl/fl) BMDMs. Upon IL-4/IL-13 stimulation, Dnmt3a-LysM BMDMs exhibited heightened ERK1/2 and PI3K signaling, reduced M2 markers, increased pro-inflammatory Irg1/Tnf transcripts, and acquired M1-like features; amplified in BMDMs from aged (>34 weeks) mice (disrupted morphology, enhanced phagocytosis, reduced arginase and elevated iNOS activity). These cells impaired epithelial regeneration in co-culture. In vivo, young Dnmt3a-LysM mice showed splenic immune alterations and DSS-colitis hypersensitivity. Aged Dnmt3a-LysM mice displayed altered bone marrow architecture, hepatosplenomegaly, and myeloproliferation. Conclusions: Dnmt3a is required for physiological macrophage polarization. Its myeloid-specific loss drives pro-inflammatory skewing, potentially contributing to IBD pathogenesis.

items.title: NOTCH3 p.R544C Drives Early Neurovascular Unit Dysfunction through Blood-Brain Barrier Failure, Complement Signalling and Metabolic Dysregulation
items.abstract: Cerebral small vessel disease is a major cause of stroke and vascular cognitive impairment, yet the mechanisms that initiate neurovascular dysfunction before irreversible brain injury remain poorly defined. CADASIL, caused by cysteine-altering NOTCH3 mutations, provides a genetically tractable model to resolve these early events. Here, we investigated the Asian-enriched NOTCH3 p.R544C variant and tested whether early disease emerges through interconnected blood-brain barrier (BBB), inflammatory, and metabolic dysfunction. NOTCH3 p.R544C iPSC-derived endothelial cells showed impaired angiogenesis and migration, reduced barrier resistance, disrupted tight-junction organisation, and altered vascular, adhesion, and extracellular-matrix programmes. In multicellular BBB-like microtissues, these defects propagated across the neurovascular unit, producing disorganised vascular networks, enlarged luminal structures, and increased permeability, establishing BBB failure as an early disease layer. Single-cell transcriptomics revealed coordinated loss of endothelial BBB transport and efflux programmes with astrocytic complement, innate immune, and matrix-remodelling activation. Secretome profiling and patient-plasma measurements converged on complement- and matrix-associated mediators, including C1S and CLU, identifying complement-matrix activation as a second interconnected layer. Importantly, combined cilostazol and isosorbide mononitrate treatment improved barrier function and reduced selected complement- and matrix-associated proteins in mutant microtissues, supporting pharmacological reversibility of components of this early disease programme. Seahorse analysis further demonstrated reduced mitochondrial respiratory capacity associated with NOTCH3 p.R544C. In vivo, three-month-old mutant mice showed altered cerebral pyruvate metabolism and early microvascular abnormalities, whereas six-month-old mice developed more prominent extracellular-matrix, inflammatory, and gliovascular changes, supporting an age-dependent transition from early metabolic dysregulation to broader neurovascular remodelling. Together, these findings define NOTCH3 p.R544C CADASIL as an early multicellular neurovascular disorder organised across three interconnected mechanistic layers: BBB failure, complement-matrix signalling, and metabolic dysregulation, while identifying early BBB-centred dysfunction as a potentially tractable state before advanced cerebrovascular injury develops.

items.title: A Beta-to-Alpha seasonal coronavirus antibody signature identifies high and low responders to SARS-CoV-2 vaccination
items.corresponding_institution: Centre for Human Genetics and Pandemic Sciences Institute, Nuffield Department of Medicine, University of Oxford, Oxford, United Kingdom
items.abstract: Pre-existing immunity to endemic seasonal human coronaviruses may shape subsequent responses to SARS-CoV-2 vaccination. We longitudinally profiled 775 healthcare workers using a systems immunology machine learning framework and found that a recursive feature elimination cross-validation model classified individuals in the top and bottom quartiles of SARS-CoV-2 Spike IgG responses (AUC=0.72, empirical P<0.001). This predictive signature was prominently driven by a baseline bias toward Beta-coronavirus relative to Alpha-coronavirus Spike reactivity.

items.title: Unexpected Long Range Actions of AAV8
items.abstract: Adeno-associated virus vectors (AAVs) have broad utility in neuroscience. A variety of features, such as titer, capsid, enhancers and promoters, coding and non-coding elements, can be utilized to pursue diverse experimental ends. The net effects of titer and capsid have been used experimentally to pursue retrograde and anterograde studies, such as through the monosynaptic spread of high-titer AAV1. The literature on AAV8 is conflicting, with evidence for and against its long-range action outside of the infected starter population. Using the mouse corticopontocerebellar tract, we report that AAV8, when used at high titers, can be associated with long range recombination outside of the starter population. This phenomenon depended upon the viral titer and was influenced by the presence of other experimental injections. Surprisingly, separate injections of high-titer AAV8 recombinase and recombinase-reporter AAV8s gave rise to recombination across long distances in populations not known to be monosynaptically connected. Given the possibility of long range and emergent effects, we suggest that investigators empirically determine titer, capsid, and injection designs that reduce false positives and/or indirect effects.

items.title: Single-base 5mC and 5hmC profiling identifies a dynamic 5hmC-to-5mC transition at gene bodies and transcription end sites during neuronal differentiation of mouse embryonic stem cells.
items.abstract: 5-methylcytosine (5mC) and 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC) are genome-wide epigenetic modifications involved in chromatin organization and transcriptional regulation. Although Enzymatic Methyl-seq (EM-seq) can enable the combined profiling of 5mC and 5hmC, Enzymatic 5hmC-seq (E5hmC-seq) can provide selective profiling of 5hmC at single-base resolution. In this context, we systematically validated E5hmC-seq using diverse genomic DNA samples. Next, we integrated E5hmC-seq with EM-seq to distinguish between 5mC and 5hmC landscapes during neuronal differentiation of mouse embryonic stem cells. First, we observed dynamic remodeling of both modifications throughout differentiation, with pronounced changes during the transition from embryoid bodies (EBs) to neural progenitor cells (NPCs), characterized by a global decrease in 5hmC accompanied by an increase in 5mC. Subsequently, differentially hydroxymethylated regions (DhMRs) exhibiting 5hmC depletion frequently showed a concurrent increase in 5mC, whereas regions gaining 5hmC displayed an opposing trend, reflecting the genome-wide relationship. Mapping these modifications to transcriptional profiles revealed an association between cytosine modification dynamics and gene expression, where transcriptional downregulation correlated with 5hmC depletion with concomitant 5mC enrichment. In summary, combined mapping of EM-seq and E5hmC-seq can decipher the dynamic interplay between 5mC and 5hmC at single-base resolution and provide insights into the relationships among cytosine modification dynamics, genomic context and transcriptional regulation during differentiation.

items.title: Distinct innate immune states associate with divergent serological outcomes after syphilis treatment
items.corresponding_institution: Hospital for Skin Diseases, Institute of Dermatology, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College
items.abstract: The global resurgence of syphilis poses a major public health challenge, even in the era of effective antibiotic therapy. Following treatment, some patients achieve seroreversion, whereas others remain serofast with persistent nontreponemal antibody reactivity. Although nontreponemal antibody titers guide clinical follow-up, it remains unclear how closely they reflect the resolution of inflammation and recovery of immune function. We integrated single-cell transcriptomics, immunophenotyping in clinical samples, and functional assays to characterize circulating monocytes and natural killer (NK) cells across seroreversion and low- and high-titer serofast states, and further examined the impact of HIV coinfection. CD14+ monocytes retained inflammatory and CD163-associated scavenging programs after seroreversion, whereas serofast patients showed additional IFN-STAT1 activation in this subset. NK cells from serofast patients exhibited reduced JUN expression and impaired degranulation. JNK inhibition reduced the magnitude and altered the kinetics of NK cell degranulation, IFN-{gamma} production, and amphiregulin (AREG) induction. Among low-titer serofast patients, HIV coinfection was associated with higher mitochondrial complex I gene expression and partially restored NK cell degranulation compared with patients with syphilis alone. Complex I inhibition also reduced NK cell degranulation. These findings suggest that seroreversion does not necessarily indicate immune normalization and identify post-treatment immune alterations not fully captured by conventional serological monitoring, providing a rationale for investigating cellular immune markers as complementary measures of recovery after syphilis treatment.

items.title: Minimal eukaryotic DNA polymerase zeta/Rev1 GC-pair mutasome
items.corresponding_institution: Eppley Institute, University of Nebraska Medical Center, Omaha, NE, USA
items.abstract: In eukaryotes, translesion DNA synthesis (TLS) enables replication across DNA lesions, difficult DNA structures, and during replicative stress. While TLS prevents replication fork collapse, it is inherently mutagenic and requires tight regulation to prevent global mutation rates increase. Here, we show that elevated DNA polymerase pol {zeta}/Rev1 promotes spontaneous mutagenesis during replication. The five subunits of pol zeta complex (pol zeta5) are the catalytic subunit Rev3, the TLS polymerase Rev1, a dimer of accessory protein Rev7, the Pol31 and Pol32 subunits shared with replicative pol delta. Pol31 and Pol32 bind the Fe-S-containing C-terminal domain (CTD) of Rev3, which serves as a major assembly hub. We found that overproduction of pol zeta5, but not four-subunit pol zeta4 lacking Rev1 or Rev1 alone, increases spontaneous mutation rates by up to 20-fold, indicating that pol zeta5 can access undamaged DNA during replication and compete with replicative DNA polymerases. This mutator effect is independent of PCNA ubiquitylation. augments by hydroxyurea and synergizes with DNA mismatch repair defects. Overproduction of a pol zeta5 complex containing CTD-truncated Rev3 is also mutagenic, demonstrating that active TLS complexes can assemble and function without the canonical CTD interaction hub. Both complexes predominantly generate CG-to-GC transversions, a mutational pattern that resembles several COSMIC cancer mutational signatures. Inactivating Rev3 catalytic activity abolishes mutagenesis, whereas loss of Rev1 catalytic activity substantially reduces mutation rates and eliminates CG-to-GC transversions, identifying Rev1 as the primary cause of the observed mutation pattern. The findings reveal previously unrecognized mechanisms of pol zeta-dependent mutagenesis with broad implications for cellular evolution and cancer development

items.title: Structural correlates of disease-associated CTSC variants in Papillon-Lefevre syndrome
items.abstract: Objective: To quantify structural features of disease-associated CTSC missense substitutions and evaluate a structural rule for research prioritization in Papillon-Lefevre syndrome. Design: We compared 16 ClinVar pathogenic or likely pathogenic missense substitutions with 234 recurrent gnomAD substitutions in the mature cathepsin C structure (PDB 1K3B). An expanded exploratory analysis included 35 further literature-indexed substitutions. We audited the documentation used to date the historical holdout and compared AlphaGenome splice scores with a consequence-only baseline. Results: Median predicted destabilization was 2.209 versus 0.763 kcal/mol (AUC 0.764, 95% CI 0.612-0.897). Catalytic proximity was observed in 4/16 versus 9/234. The expanded comparison gave AUC 0.740. Sixteen of 31 substitutions in the historical post-2015 subset had references dated through 2015. For noncoding variants, AlphaGenome splice scores and the consequence-only baseline both obtained AUC 1.000 on 12 positive and 105 negative ClinVar records. Conclusions: Predicted destabilization was associated with ClinVar label status in this dataset. The literature chronology and noncoding consequence composition limit claims of predictive validation.

items.title: Short intervals of inertial measurement unit data collected during activities of daily living can provide a quantitative method to assess disease severity and functional ability in Parkinson's disease
items.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder affecting roughly one million people in the U.S. People with PD (PwPD) exhibit classic motor symptoms that limit performance on functional tasks and reduce quality of life (QOL). Despite functional ability (FA) being a critical indicator of patient well-being, objective and quantitative measurement of FA during activities of daily living (ADLs) is not a part of standard clinical assessments. To address this gap, we conducted a pilot study of PwPD (n = 39) and healthy controls (n = 7) performing ADLs. We attached nine-axis inertial measurement units (IMUs) to toothbrushes and hair combs to collect continuous acceleration and angular velocity data during toothbrushing and hair-combing tasks. After preprocessing, we visualized signals with kernel density estimation and continuous wavelet transforms, revealing characteristic distributional, temporal, and spectral patterns. We then segmented signals into 3-9 second non-overlapping intervals. From each interval, we extracted 30 features (13 acceleration-derived, 17 angular-velocity-derived) and trained eXtreme Gradient Boosted (XGBoost) classifiers to discriminate disease state and severity, symptom presence, and impaired FA. Notably, models trained on hair-combing data discriminated PwPD from controls (balanced accuracy 0.864) and identified patient-reported impairment in FA (0.869). Models trained on toothbrushing data achieved moderate performance on the same tasks (balanced accuracy 0.752 and 0.686, respectively). These preliminary findings suggest that short-segment IMU data from common ADL implements can quantitatively characterize disease severity and task-specific performance in PwPD, supporting their integration into routine clinical care.
